question: Compare JWT access tokens and server-side sessions for a same-site web app.
shortAnswer: Sessions store authoritative state server-side (easy revoke); JWTs are self-contained (harder revoke) and need careful storage/TTL.
strongAnswer: Server sessions typically place an opaque id in an HttpOnly cookie and look up session data centrally—logout/revocation is straightforward. JWTs encode claims and can be validated without a store, which helps scale, but revocation before expiry needs extra infrastructure; use short-lived access tokens and careful cookie/XSS posture. Neither is automatically more secure.
followUps: Why is localStorage risky for tokens?
How does refresh token rotation help?
commonWrongAnswer: JWTs are always more secure than sessions.
productionRelevance: Wrong choice complicates logout, XSS impact, and horizontal scaling.
integrationProcedure: 1) Reproduce the scenario in a small spike using JWT, HTTP, Cookies. 2) Write the strong answer as an ADR or PR description. 3) Add a test or monitor that would catch the common wrong answer in production. 4) Document rollback/owner. 5) Rehearse the follow-ups aloud once.
